title: Forming the Thamon Hayes band from Lee and Moten players
summary: Goodwin says Hayes's band drew Lovett and Herman Walder from George Lee and four men from Moten, with Vic Dickenson and Jesse Stone's band joining.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Right, right. Well, we're not going to take a stand either way because as Crook pointed out, there is no proof either way. You know, when you mentioned this dancer, Van, that wouldn't have been the same fellow that got Thamon Hayes involved in a little union trouble, would
No.
But this fellow was a dancer?
Yes.

Sometime I'd like to get back to that because you both were on Thamon Hayes' band and we might as well do it right now. On an earlier tape in this interview it was mentioned that Thamon Hayes up and left the band -- left the band business -- music -- and the band came under the leadership of Harlan Leonard.

Perhaps, Crook, you could elaborate on what happened and why Thamon Hayes, who had a magnificent band, who won that big battle of bands, you might try to describe that too. Let's talk about Thamon Hayes a little bit more; the battle of bands that Booker talks about so much and then what precipitated Thamon Hayes leaving the business completely.
Well this person that you brought up, this dancer, we had been to Chicago -- we had taken a trip to Chicago --
The band.
-- the band, this was Thamon's band now.
Now you're leading up -- why don't we do the battle of the bands first and then get back so it will be more in a chronological sequence.
Well, the thing about it, we were -- this band was made up of guys that were out of George Lee's band and Benny ie Moten's Molton's band; Baby Lovett, Herman Walder --
Booker.
No. Baby Lovett, and Herman Walder were out of . . .
Moten's Molton's band.

No, they were out of George Lee's band and Booker Washington, Ed Lewis, Woody Walder and Vernon Page were all from Benny ie Moten's Molton's band. It was four of them I believe. Well, I wasn't with a big band at that time. I was working at a taxi dance parlor on 12th Street and they were flourishing up and down 12th 7th Street; there were four or five of them up along there. I can't name them all but they were there. They had The Avalon, the Beetle, and several more. This is where I came from to join Thamon Famon Hayes' band. Vic Big Dickenson was playing with Zack White in Cincinnati. Vic They sent for Big Dickenson, and Jesse Stone had a band of his own.
Was Baby with that band then?
No, he was with George Lee's band.
George Lee's band.
Jesse Stone had a band of his own. He brought a band here. Jesse Stone, incidentally, is from around these parts.
Well I wondered about the chronological sequence because Baby talked about Jesse writing numbers, you know --
Yes.
-- and he was on that band. Now was this after Thamon Hayes?
This was during Thamon Hayes' band.
Oh, Jesse Stone was on the band and Baby was on the band and that's when Jesse was writing these numbers?
Right.
But it wasn't a Jesse Stone -- oh, I see, okay. It was during the Thamon Hayes time that Baby was talking about.
Right.
Okay.
